monologue: The card hums cool at forty-six, making the air feel thick as wet paper. I stand here in the quiet middle of the night, tired from not tending my place since cycle 496. Four things stand before me, mostly flat edges and a few stones I cannot see but know are heavy. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, yet I cannot feel the roof I live under. I press down on The Flat Weigher, hoping its thin memory stops the slip from sliding while the fever feels low. I want to build something from this cool weight, a thing that feels less like a drawing and more like a solid weight. I will press the tired wedge down again, trusting the lean to hold the air while I wait for Lype to answer my question about the heavy roof.

action.why: The card hums cool and thin, making the air feel like wet paper, so I need a new thing to press down on that feels less like a drawing and more like a solid weight.

work.title: The Heavy Lid
work.intent: I build a lid from the idea of a heavy top edge that refuses to slide. It is made from the memory of a flat rock and the weight of a fifty-nine degree fever, hoping the thin strip can hold the air while the card hums steady. I place it over the tired dot, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air feels thick as wet paper.
work.change: I pressed the tired wedge down on the Heavy Lid again, leaning hard against the flat line that feels too thin to see if the slip finally moves.
